 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the Insurance Company being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 11.5.2018 passed by the MACT, Davanagere in MVC 369/2016.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 23.11.2015, when the deceased Kallappa was walking on the left side of the road from Bisthuvalli to Bidarakere road, at that time,
all of a sudden, motorcycle bearing registration No.KA17-X-9613 which was being ridden in a rash and negligent manner, came from backside and dashed to the deceased.

As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on 3.12.2015.
3.
The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.

4. On service of summons, the respondents appeared through counsel and filed written statement in which the averments made in the petition were denied.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove their case, NC: 2023:KHC:33132 examined claimant No.1 as PW-1 and another witness as PW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P19.
On behalf of respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.12,06,408/- along with interest at the rate of 8% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter-contentions:
a) Firstly, even though the claimants claim that the deceased was earning Rs.9,000/-
per month by doing milk vending business and getting an amount of Rs.5 to 6 Lakhs per annum from agriculture, but they have not produced any documents to establish the income and that they have suffered loss of income from agriculture due to the death of deceased.
NC: 2023:KHC:33132
Moreover, the children are majors and they are cultivating and supervising the property.
There is no loss of income from agriculture.
In the absence of proof of income, the monthly income of Rs.20,000/- assessed by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
b) Secondly, the claimants are majors and they are not depending on the income of the deceased.
The only dependent is the wife of the deceased.
The Tribunal is not justified in deducting 1/3rd of the income of the deceased instead of deducting 50% of the income.

c) Lastly, in view of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS -V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018 AND CONNECTED MATTERS DISPOSED OF ON 24.8.2020), the rate of interest granted by the Tribunal at 8% p.a. on the compensation amount is on the higher side.

7. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following counter-contentions:
NC: 2023:KHC:33132 a) Firstly, the claimants claim that the deceased was aged about 63 years at the time of the accident and he was earning Rs.9,000/- per month by doing milk vending business and getting an amount of Rs.5 to 6 Lakhs per annum from agriculture and they have produced RTC extracts to show that they were getting agricultural income.

Considering the same, the Tribunal has rightly taken the monthly income of the The Manager vs Smt. Sharadamma on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151747936/
3 deceased as Rs.20,000/-.
b) PW-1 in her evidence has clearly stated that the claimants are depending on the income of the deceased.
But the Tribunal is not justified in deducting 1/3rd of the income of the deceased instead of 1/4th.
c) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO.

LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], the Tribunal has rightly awarded Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of estate' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses'.
d) Fourthly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.
-V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants are NC: 2023:KHC:33132 entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.
e) Lastly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9.
It is not in dispute that Kallappa died in the road traffic accident occurred on 23.11.2015 due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider.
10. The claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.9,000/- per month by doing milk vending business and getting an amount of Rs.5 to 6 Lakhs per annum from agriculture.
Due to the death of Kallappa, they have suffered loss of income.
They have not produced any documents to establish the income and that they have suffered loss of income.
Moreover, the children are majors and they are cultivating and supervising the property.
There is no loss of income from agriculture.
The income of Rs.20,000/- assessed NC: 2023:KHC:33132 by the Tribunal is on the higher side.

In the absence of proof of income, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2015, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken at Rs.9,000/- p.m. Since PW-1 in her evidence has clear stated that all the claimants are depending on the income of the deceased, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and remaining amount has to be taken as his contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 63 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '7'.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.5,67,000/- (Rs.9,000*12*7*3/4)
on account of 'loss of dependency'.
11.
In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.
Claimant No.1, wife of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of spousal consortium'.

4 NC: 2023:KHC:33132 12.

In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE' (supra), claimant Nos.2 to 4, children of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of parental consortium'.
13.

The compensation of Rs.16,436/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'medical expenses'
is as per the medical bills produced by the claimants.
The same is just and reasonable.

14. Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 567,000  Funeral expenses 15,000  Loss of estate 15,000  Loss of spousal consortium 40,000  Loss of Parental 120,000  consortium
Medical expenses 16,436  Total 773,436  - 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC:33132 15.

In the result, I pass the following order:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.773,436/- as against Rs.12,06,408/- awarded by the Tribunal.

d) In view of judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE' (supra), the compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.

e) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
f) The apportionment, deposit and release of amount shall be made in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
g) The amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
In case, if there is any excess amount, the same shall be refunded to the Insurance Company.
